---
title: "ECON 000 --- Your Course Title"
author: "Your Name"

# `term:`, not `date:`. Quarto parses `date:` as a calendar date and
# normalises it, so "Fall 2026" would render as 2026-01-01. before-body.tex
# passes `term:` straight to LaTeX's \date{}, so it prints as written --
# in the title block and in the running head.
term: "Fall 2026"

# Course information block. Every key below is optional -- anything you
# omit renders as TBD in the table under the title, so the block keeps its
# shape while the term is still being scheduled.
#
# `web:` takes a BARE host. before-body.tex supplies the https:// prefix,
# so writing a full URL here produces https://https://... in the link.
email: your.name@example.edu
web: canvas.example.edu
officehours: "Tuesdays 14:00--16:00, or by appointment"
classhours: "Monday and Wednesday, 10:30--11:50"
office: "Social Sciences Building, Office 512"
classroom: "Social Sciences Building, Room 203"

# Institution logo, centred above the title. logo.pdf is a placeholder --
# swap in your own file (PDF, PNG or JPG) and keep the name, or point this
# key elsewhere. Deleting the key drops the logo and the title block
# closes up; deleting the FILE while this key still points at it is a hard
# render error, not a warning.
logo: logo.pdf
# logo-width: '0.30\textwidth'

# The reading list at the end is generated from every entry in
# references.bib, because of `nocite: "@*"`. Drop that key to list only
# the works actually cited in the body.
bibliography: references.bib
nocite: |
  @*

# Citations go through natbib/BibTeX rather than Quarto's default
# CSL/citeproc, matching the qkit paper template. natbib hyperlinks both
# halves of an author-year citation, so the whole of "Campbell and Shiller
# (1988)" is clickable, and it means titles in references.bib have to be
# double-braced. `apalike` is deliberate: it ships in TeX Live base, so it
# resolves under the TinyTeX install Quarto uses as well as a full
# TeX Live. The heading over the generated list is \refname, set in
# preamble.tex -- Quarto's `reference-section-title` does nothing here.
cite-method: natbib
biblio-style: apalike
natbiboptions: round,authoryear
link-citations: true

format:
  pdf:
    # pdflatex, not the xelatex the qkit paper template uses. mathpazo is
    # a pdftex-era font package, and Pandoc only honours `fontfamily:` on
    # the pdftex path -- under xelatex or lualatex it loads fontspec and
    # ignores the key, so the syllabus would silently render in Latin
    # Modern. Switch both lines together if you want a different face.
    pdf-engine: pdflatex
    fontfamily: mathpazo
    documentclass: article
    classoption:
      - "11pt"
    geometry:
      - margin=1in
    fontsize: 11pt
    linestretch: 1.05
    number-sections: false
    colorlinks: true
    linkcolor: black
    citecolor: blue
    urlcolor: blue
    template-partials:
      - before-body.tex
    include-in-header: preamble.tex
---

# Course Description

This is a self-documenting syllabus template. Each section below both
demonstrates a piece of the layout and explains how to change it ---
replace the demonstration text with your own as you fill it in.

Open the YAML header above first. The title, author and term come from
`title:`, `author:` and `term:`, and the title and term also drive the
running head at the top of every page after this one. The six-field
table under the title is built from `email:`, `web:`, `officehours:`,
`classhours:`, `office:` and `classroom:`. Delete any of those keys and
the corresponding cell reads *TBD*; there is no LaTeX to edit for
routine changes.

Write the real course description here: what the course is about, why it
matters, and what a student who finishes it will be able to do. Two or
three paragraphs is the usual length.

# Objectives

By the end of the course, students will be able to:

1. State the first learning objective in terms of what the student can
   *do*, not what the course *covers*.

2. State the second objective.

3. State the third objective.

4. State the fourth objective.

5. State the fifth objective.

Keep the list to five or six entries. Lists here are ordinary markdown,
and the numbering is automatic --- inserting an objective in the middle
renumbers the rest.

# Prerequisites and Materials

**Prerequisites.** List the courses or the background a student needs
before enrolling, along with any placement requirement or instructor
permission.

**Software.** List everything students must install, with versions and a
link to the download page --- for example the course computing
environment [@toolmaker2024software] together with an IDE. Say
explicitly whether the software is free, and whether lab machines have
it preinstalled.

**Readings.** The list at the end of this document is generated from
`references.bib` and headed *Recommended Readings*. Every entry shipped
there is a placeholder --- invented authors and titles --- so replace
them with your own. Cite a work inline with `@author2020textbook`,
which renders as a parenthetical citation, or with
`[@researcher2018article]` for a bracketed one; both halves of the
citation are clickable and link down to the entry. Because
`nocite: "@*"` is set in the header, every entry in the `.bib` file is
listed whether or not it is cited --- which is normally what a syllabus
wants. Remove that key to list only the works you actually cite.

# Methodology

Describe how the course runs: lectures, seminars, problem sessions, lab
work, or some mix. Say what students are expected to do before each
meeting, and how class time will actually be spent.

# Grading

The final grade is weighted as follows:

| Component | Weight | Notes |
|:----------|-------:|:------|
| Problem sets | 40% | Five sets, lowest score dropped |
| Midterm exam | 25% | In class, closed book |
| Final exam | 30% | Cumulative |
| Participation | 5% | Attendance and in-class exercises |

Weights must sum to 100%. Add a sentence here on the grading scale, on
whether grades are curved, and on the procedure for requesting a
regrade.

# Course Schedule

The schedule is a markdown pipe table. Pandoc renders these as
`longtable`, so a schedule longer than a page breaks across pages
rather than overflowing --- which is what you want here. The
`tbl-colwidths` attribute sets the column proportions; without it the
topic column gets squeezed by the longer reading entries.

| Week | Dates | Topic | Readings and Deliverables |
|:-----|:------|:------|:--------------------------|
| 1 | Aug 24 -- Aug 28 | Introduction and course logistics | --- |
| 2 | Aug 31 -- Sep 04 | First substantive topic | Ch. 1--2 |
| 3 | Sep 07 -- Sep 11 | Second substantive topic | Ch. 3; PS 1 due |
| 4 | Sep 14 -- Sep 18 | Third substantive topic | Ch. 4 |
| 5 | Sep 21 -- Sep 25 | Fourth substantive topic | PS 2 due |
| 6 | Sep 28 -- Oct 02 | Review and midterm exam | Midterm, Oct 02 |
| 7 | Oct 05 -- Oct 09 | Fifth substantive topic | Ch. 5--6 |
| 8 | Oct 12 -- Oct 16 | Sixth substantive topic | PS 3 due |
| 9 | Oct 19 -- Oct 23 | Seventh substantive topic | Ch. 7 |
| 10 | Oct 26 -- Oct 30 | Synthesis and final review | PS 4 due |

: Course schedule {#tbl-schedule tbl-colwidths="[8,22,42,28]"}

Refer to the schedule with `@tbl-schedule`, which renders as
@tbl-schedule. Never put a literal "Table" in front of the reference:
Quarto supplies that prefix itself, so `Table @tbl-schedule` comes out
as *Table Table 1*.

# Course Contents

The detailed outline, as a nested list. Numbers and letters are
generated, so reordering a unit does not mean renumbering by hand.

# Course Policies

## Academic Integrity

State the institution's academic-integrity policy and what it means in
this course specifically: which work must be individual, what
collaboration is permitted on problem sets, whether generative AI tools
may be used and how their use must be disclosed, and what the
consequences of a violation are.

## Late Work

State the deadline convention, the penalty for late submission, and the
circumstances under which an extension is granted along with who to ask
and how far in advance.

## Attendance

State whether attendance is recorded, whether it affects the grade, and
what a student should do after missing a class.

## Accessibility and Accommodations

State how students register an accommodation with the relevant office
and how far in advance the instructor needs the paperwork. Name the
office and give its contact details rather than pointing at the policy
in the abstract.
